global_caption: The video contains 8 shots and is a narrative short film in low-saturation anime espionage style, set in a post-apocalyptic wasteland featuring abandoned stations and ruined districts. The visual palette is dominated by cold gray tones, enhanced with dark high-contrast lighting and sparse backlight dust haze.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with fade-in from black, wide shot, overhead angle, first establishing the full view of the ruined city. Broken overpasses and tilted buildings form diagonal leading lines. Foreground features a twisted section of barbed wire. Midground shows an anthropomorphic tiger wearing a tattered cloak moving quickly along a collapsed street. In the background, flickering remnants of signage are blown by wind. Natural cool light is diffused by thick dust, leaving only narrow bright edges on steel beams. The character moves cautiously, cloak hem and tail fluttering in the wind. The camera slightly tilts down and slowly follows forward. A crisp metallic clink echoes as boots step on metal fragments, layered with distant wind.
shot2: Shot 2 enters via hard cut from previous shot, close-up, eye-level framing, closely following the protagonist’s upper body. Composition places the subject in left-side shadow, right side reserved for the dark entrance of the old station. Shallow depth of field blurs peeling walls and rusted timetables in the background. The protagonist ducks into the abandoned waiting area, stops against a broken pillar, cloak slipping slightly open. Claws retrieve a creased code paper from an inner pocket; its edge trembles in the cold wind. A localized top light slices across claws and paper, creating high-contrast chiaroscuro blocks. The camera subtly pushes in, emphasizing the cautious pause during retrieval.
shot3: Shot 3 cuts via action match to extreme close-up, overhead angle, focusing on the damaged telegraph machine and the protagonist’s claws. A blurred severed wire passes through foreground; background sinks into darkness. The code paper rests on a rust-stained surface. Claws press keys one by one, tiny pauses, rebounds, and mechanical vibrations clearly visible. Numbers are rapidly matched, marked, and confirmed on paper. The telegraph’s edge reveals worn texture under harsh side lighting. The camera remains nearly static, with minimal push-in to amplify focus.
shot4: Column rows create obstruction and voyeuristic feel. Rusty columns sweep across foreground; midground gradually reveals the platform end. The second anthropomorphic tiger never fully enters center frame—only briefly pauses beneath an inspection sign, gently placing half a metal badge on the edge of a peeling bench, then retreating into shadow. The badge flashes briefly under a narrow beam of cold light, becoming the sole prominent focal point. Wind shakes hanging signs, producing intermittent rattles. A partially open iron door in distance flaps gently, building suspense for the contact’s appearance.
shot5: Shot 5 enters via hard cut from previous shot, close-up, eye-level, using intersecting lateral motion. Two tigers enter from left and right, briefly overlapping at the boundary of platform light and shadow. Blurred railing in foreground creates thin obstruction. Background shows the dark side of a long-stationed train. As protagonist leans past the bench, it picks up half the badge. The approaching tiger lifts its paw slightly at the moment of passing, handing over the code strip. They never make eye contact or stop—exchange completed via shoulder lines, paw gestures, and cloak movement. Actions are brief but precise; fabric edges and tails trail naturally with steps. Camera synchronously pushes in slightly then shifts horizontally, intensifying “擦身而过”’s sense of danger.
shot6: Shot 6 begins with abrupt hard cut to create alertness, switching to full shot, overhead angle, showing entire meeting zone from above the platform. Tracks, debris, and cover form geometric divisions. A patrol spotlight suddenly sweeps across the center, instantly illuminating dust and two silhouettes. Both tigers simultaneously lower their centers of gravity—one slides behind an overturned cargo box, the other rolls into shadow beside a broken wall. Movement paths clearly diverge toward separate covers. Dust rises into a thin haze. In alternating light and dark, taut muscles and cloak hems show instant tension. Camera slightly dips down then pulls back gently, emphasizing exposure. Iron door creaks here are amplified, syncing rhythmically with the spotlight sweep, reinforcing pressure.
shot7: Shot 7 cuts via transition from light to dark zone, close-up, overhead angle, returning to protagonist’s cover interior. Framing places broken concrete blocks at foreground edge, creating enclosure. Focus is on protagonist’s claws and two halves of code components. In tight shadow, protagonist quickly joins half-badge and code strip, cross-referencing with earlier code paper to confirm evacuation coordinates. Circled numbers and simplified route diagrams appear sequentially under faint side light. Protagonist’s ear twitches, eyes lift—shift from cautious probing to decisive action. Camera performs short push-in, centering the completion of assembly as key narrative moment.
shot8: Shot 8 continues from previous shot via fade-in to wide shot, slight upward angle, scene shifting to exterior of derelict train. Foreground: gravel and sleepers. Midground: protagonist leaps onto train roof using wreckage. Background: wasteland horizon swallowed by dust. Backlight cuts diagonally from behind the train, outlining protagonist as sharp silhouette. Leap, landing, turn to check direction, then sprint forward—all in one fluid motion. Dust particles rise and form fine light trails in high-contrast lighting. Rusty surface and cracked edges of train are clearly visible in final highlights. Camera first tilts up slightly to follow leap, then slowly pulls back, letting character gradually vanish into dust and backlight. Escape completes as conclusion. Wind dominates final Final image lingers on empty tracks and swaying broken signs.
